title: "Deploying models"
subtitle: "Create a callable service file for a fitted workflow"
description: "Learn how vetiver records a fitted text model, writes an API file, and preserves evaluation details before deployment."
categories: [model development, deployment, vetiver]
---

A data team has sufficient evaluation evidence to examine a model before deployment.
Another system now needs to submit a paragraph and receive a label.

Deployment packages the fitted object, expected input structure, and calling
code. It does not improve the model.

The deployment record also needs the evaluation evidence that justifies the
model's operation. An API does not establish that its answers are correct.

::: {.callout-tip}
## What you will learn

This lesson shows how to:

- wrap a fitted tidymodels workflow with vetiver.
- pin the model to a local board.
- examine the prototype input saved with the model.
- write the Plumber API file without starting a server.
- name the evaluation details that must accompany a deployed model.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false

options(warn = 2)
stopifnot(identical(getOption("warn"), 2L))
```

## Fit the model to be packaged

A deployment needs the exact fitted object evaluated. Here the
object is the era classifier from a speech-held-out split with seed `4301` and
fit seed `4302`.

Production teams often refit an evaluated model design on all available
labelled data. This lesson instead packages the held-out fit. That choice
links the stored object to its exact live score and makes its provenance easier
to examine. A full-data refit creates a new object. Its evaluation evidence
comes from earlier fits with the same design rather than a score for that new
object.

```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(readr)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tibble)
  library(stringr)
  library(rsample)
  library(recipes)
  library(textrecipes)
  library(parsnip)
  library(workflows)
  library(yardstick)
  library(vetiver)
  library(pins)
  library(glmnet)
})

source("R/inaugural-corpus.R")
paragraphs <- inaugural_paragraphs()

study <- read_csv(
  "data/inaugural/split-study.csv",
  na = c("", "NA"),
  col_types = cols(
    task = col_character(),
    split_scheme = col_character(),
    replicate = col_integer(),
    accuracy = col_double(),
    bal_accuracy = col_double(),
    train_majority_accuracy = col_double(),
    test_majority_rate = col_double(),
    length_rule_accuracy = col_double(),
    test_rows = col_integer(),
    test_speeches = col_integer()
  )
)

set.seed(4301)
era_split <- group_initial_split(paragraphs, group = speech_id, prop = 0.75)
era_training <- training(era_split)
era_testing <- testing(era_split)

era_recipe <- recipe(era ~ paragraph, data = era_training) |>
  step_tokenize(paragraph) |>
  step_stopwords(paragraph) |>
  step_tokenfilter(paragraph, max_tokens = 500) |>
  step_tfidf(paragraph)

era_model <- logistic_reg(penalty = 0.01, mixture = 0) |>
  set_engine("glmnet")

era_workflow <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(era_recipe) |>
  add_model(era_model)

set.seed(4302)
era_fitted <- fit(era_workflow, data = era_training)

era_predictions <- predict(era_fitted, era_testing) |>
  bind_cols(era_testing |> select(era))

live_accuracy <- accuracy(
  era_predictions,
  truth = era,
  estimate = .pred_class
) |>
  pull(.estimate)

training_majority <- era_training |>
  count(era, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice(1) |>
  pull(era)
live_majority_accuracy <- mean(era_testing$era == training_majority)

speech_summary <- study |>
  filter(task == "era", split_scheme == "speech") |>
  summarise(
    model_accuracy = mean(accuracy),
    train_majority_accuracy = mean(train_majority_accuracy),
    length_rule_accuracy = mean(length_rule_accuracy),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

evaluation_date <- as.Date("2026-08-29")
deployment_record <- tibble(
  record = c(
    "data source",
    "selected candidate",
    "selected penalty",
    "selection resampling",
    "split scheme",
    "training paragraphs",
    "test paragraphs",
    "live test accuracy",
    "live train-majority baseline",
    "speech-split mean accuracy",
    "speech-split mean train-majority baseline",
    "speech-split mean length baseline",
    "evaluation date"
  ),
  value = c(
    "inaugural paragraphs",
    "ridge logistic regression",
    "0.01",
    "five folds grouped by speech inside training",
    "speech_id group split",
    as.character(nrow(era_training)),
    as.character(nrow(era_testing)),
    as.character(round(live_accuracy, 4)),
    as.character(round(live_majority_accuracy, 4)),
    as.character(round(speech_summary$model_accuracy, 4)),
    as.character(round(speech_summary$train_majority_accuracy, 4)),
    as.character(round(speech_summary$length_rule_accuracy, 4)),
    as.character(evaluation_date)
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  deployment_record,
  col.names = c("Record item", "Value"),
  caption = "Evaluation details kept beside the deployable model",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  identical(nrow(era_training), 1042L),
  identical(nrow(era_testing), 335L),
  identical(round(live_accuracy, 4), 0.8209),
  identical(round(live_majority_accuracy, 4), 0.4179),
  identical(round(speech_summary$model_accuracy, 4), 0.8457),
  identical(round(speech_summary$train_majority_accuracy, 4), 0.6282),
  identical(round(speech_summary$length_rule_accuracy, 4), 0.6827),
  identical(evaluation_date, as.Date("2026-08-29")),
  identical(nrow(deployment_record), 13L)
)
```

Deployment records a specific model version. The record names the object's
data split, score, and comparison baseline. The repeated speech-split study
provides additional context because one split can have an unusual class mix.

## Pin the fitted workflow

`vetiver_model()` combines the fitted workflow with metadata. A **prototype**
is the empty input table that records the model's expected columns. A local
**pins board** stores versioned objects. This lesson uses a project-local
scratch board and removes it after reading the generated files.

```{r}
make_api_artifacts <- function(fitted_model) {
  board_dir <- file.path("9_model_development", ".lesson-46-board")
  api_file <- file.path("9_model_development", ".lesson-46-api.R")
  unlink(c(board_dir, api_file), recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE)
  dir.create(board_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  on.exit(unlink(c(board_dir, api_file), recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE), add = TRUE)

  vetiver_object <- suppressMessages(
    vetiver_model(fitted_model, "inaugural-era-workflow")
  )
  board <- board_folder(board_dir, versioned = TRUE)
  capture.output(
    suppressMessages(vetiver_pin_write(board, vetiver_object))
  )
  versions <- pin_versions(board, "inaugural-era-workflow")
  pinned_model <- vetiver_pin_read(
    board,
    "inaugural-era-workflow",
    version = versions$version[[1]]
  )

  suppressMessages(
    vetiver_write_plumber(
      board,
      "inaugural-era-workflow",
      version = versions$version[[1]],
      file = api_file
    )
  )
  api_lines <- read_lines(api_file)
  board_path <- str_match(api_lines[str_detect(api_lines, "board_folder")], 'path = "([^"]+)"')[, 2]
  if (length(board_path) == 0L || is.na(board_path[[1]])) {
    board_path <- ""
  }
  display_lines <- api_lines
  if (nzchar(board_path)) {
    display_lines <- display_lines |>
      str_replace_all(stringr::fixed(board_path), "<local board path>")
  }
  display_lines <- display_lines |>
    str_replace_all(stringr::fixed(versions$version[[1]]), "<pinned version>")

  list(
    vetiver_object = vetiver_object,
    versions = versions,
    pinned_model = pinned_model,
    api_lines = api_lines,
    display_lines = display_lines
  )
}

api_artifacts <- make_api_artifacts(era_fitted)
vetiver_object <- api_artifacts$vetiver_object
versions <- api_artifacts$versions
pinned_model <- api_artifacts$pinned_model
prototype_table <- tibble(
  columns = paste(names(vetiver_object$prototype), collapse = ", "),
  rows = nrow(vetiver_object$prototype)
)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  prototype_table,
  col.names = c("Prototype columns", "Prototype rows"),
  caption = "Input shape stored with the vetiver model",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  identical(vetiver_object$model_name, "inaugural-era-workflow"),
  identical(names(vetiver_object$prototype), "paragraph"),
  identical(nrow(vetiver_object$prototype), 0L),
  identical(prototype_table$columns, "paragraph"),
  identical(prototype_table$rows, 0L),
  identical(nrow(versions), 1L),
  identical(pinned_model$model_name, vetiver_object$model_name)
)
```

The version lets a later system ask for this exact object. The prototype says the
API expects a table with a `paragraph` column. The pinned board is the place the
API reads from when it starts.

## Write the API file without starting it

`vetiver_write_plumber()` writes an R file for a Plumber API. This lesson only
writes and reads that file. It does not start a server and it makes no network
request.

```{r}
#| output: asis

api_lines <- api_artifacts$api_lines
display_lines <- api_artifacts$display_lines

cat("```r\n", paste(display_lines, collapse = "\n"), "\n```\n", sep = "")
```

```{r}
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  length(api_lines) >= 20L,
  any(str_detect(api_lines, stringr::fixed("vetiver_api(v)"))),
  any(str_detect(api_lines, stringr::fixed("vetiver_pin_read"))),
  any(str_detect(api_lines, stringr::fixed("inaugural-era-workflow"))),
  any(str_detect(api_lines, stringr::fixed("@plumber"))),
  any(str_detect(api_lines, stringr::fixed("library(plumber)"))),
  !any(str_detect(display_lines, stringr::fixed(versions$version[[1]]))),
  any(str_detect(display_lines, stringr::fixed("<pinned version>")))
)
```

vetiver generates the file shown above. The display replaces the local board
path and version string with placeholders so the rendered lesson remains
stable. The assertions examine the generated file before those replacements.

A deployment record needs the selected candidate, settings, data source, split
scheme, score, baseline, and date. This example uses ridge logistic regression
with penalty `0.01` on inaugural paragraphs. Its split holds out whole speeches.

The live accuracy is `r round(live_accuracy, 4)`. The same-split
training-majority baseline is `r round(live_majority_accuracy, 4)`. The
evaluation date is `r as.character(evaluation_date)`. The fixed seeds are
`4301` and `4302`.

The party model with this recipe and penalty did not pass evaluation.
Do not deploy it through an API. Packaging makes access easier but does not
correct a failed measurement.

## What to remember

- Deployment packages a fitted object so another system can call it.
- A vetiver prototype records the input columns the model expects.
- A pins board stores model versions.
- Do not deploy a model that did not pass evaluation.
- Keep the candidate, settings, data, split, score, baseline, and date with the
  deployed object.

An API lets another system request model predictions. Its documentation must
also preserve the model's limits.
